We need count of methyl groups in the molecule. But we have no description of molecule. Possibly need to get NMR spectra and infer? But we don't know which molecule. Maybe the sample is implicit? Could be the molecule under investigation is the one for which we can get NMR spectra via tools without parameters. The tools carbon_nmr_spectra, proton_nmr_spectra, hsqc_nmr_spectra take no arguments. So they will return spectra for "sample at hand". Likely the environment has a hidden molecule. We need count of methyl groups. We can get proton NMR to see signals for CH3 (singlet ~0.9 ppm). But need to deduce number of methyl groups. Could also get carbon NMR to see number of methyl carbon signals (~10-30 ppm). But need count of methyl groups, not distinct signals (could be equivalent). Might need HSQC to correlate.

Simplify: Use proton NMR to count number of methyl protons (3H each). But overlapping signals may be ambiguous. However we can also get carbon NMR to count methyl carbons.

Probably easiest: carbon_nmr_spectra returns list of chemical shifts? Let's call it.
